{{Short description|None}}
At a global level, men represent both the majority of victims and the majority of perpetrators of homicide. According to the 2023 [[United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime|UNODC]] Global Study on Homicide, in 2021, at a global level, 81% of homicide victims were men.<ref>{{Cite web | quote=In 2021, more than 8 out of 10 homicide victims worldwide were men and boys (81 per cent) while fewer than 2 out of 10 were women and girls (19 per cent) [...] In 2021, just a handful of countries recorded more female homicide victims than male homicide victims [...] Austria, Czechia, Iceland, Latvia, Norway, Slovenia and Switzerland | page=56 | url=https://www.unodc.org/documents/data-and-analysis/gsh/2023/Global_study_on_homicide_2023_web.pdf | title=Global study on homicide 2023 | website=www.unodc.org}}</ref> In 2021, males accounted for most homicide victims in all jurisdictions except in [[Austria]], the [[Czech Republic]], [[Iceland]], [[Latvia]], [[Norway]], [[Slovenia]] and [[Switzerland]], where females were slightly more likely to be homicide victims.<ref name="unodc">{{Cite web | url=https://www.unodc.org/documents/data-and-analysis/gsh/2023/Global_study_on_homicide_2023_web.pdf | title=Global study on homicide 2023 | website=www.unodc.org}}</ref> The global homicide rate was 9.3 per 100,000 males and 2.2 per 100,000 females;  and 90% of homicide suspects brought into formal contact with the police were men.<ref name="unodc" /> According to the most recent data from [[World Bank Group]], the highest rate per 100,000 inhabitants for female homicide victims is in [[Central African Republic]], [[Antigua and Barbuda]] and [[Jamaica]],<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/VC.IHR.PSRC.FE.P5?most_recent_value_desc=true|title=Intentional homicides, female (per 100,000 female)|website=World Bank Open Data}}</ref> and the highest rate per 100,000 inhabitants for male homicide victims is in [[US Virgin Islands]], [[Jamaica]] and [[Venezuela]].<ref name="auto"/> In 2020, the average percentage of women as homicide victims among [[European Union]] countries was 37%, with Latvia having the largest percentage of women homicide victims at 60%.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Latvia still leads EU on homicides, particularly of women / Article | url=https://eng.lsm.lv/article/society/crime/latvia-still-leads-eu-on-homicides-particularly-of-women.a460574/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220608183912/https://eng.lsm.lv/article/society/crime/latvia-still-leads-eu-on-homicides-particularly-of-women.a460574/ | access-date=2026-02-14 | archive-date=2022-06-08}}</ref>

The pattern of males constituting both the majority of perpetrators and of victims has been also observed in studies recording lethal violence in [[chimpanzees]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=Chimpanzee males more likely to kill and be killed | url=https://www.mpg.de/8430864/chimpanzee-males-aggression | access-date=2026-02-14 | website=www.mpg.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | title=Chimpanzees and death {{!}} Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B {{!}} The Royal Society | url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rstb/article/373/1754/20170257/23519/Chimpanzees-and-deathChimpanzees-and-death | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107170556/https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rstb/article/373/1754/20170257/23519/Chimpanzees-and-deathChimpanzees-and-death | access-date=2026-02-14 | archive-date=2026-01-07}}</ref>
